No pharmacokinetic interaction is anticipated with short-term albendazole use, but its clinical efficacy may diminish with prolonged treatment. 3. Co-administration may increase tenofovir alafenamide exposure. Consider using a 10 mg daily dose of tenofovir alafenamide where available. 4. Co-administration may elevate tenofovir exposure. Monitor for adverse reactions associated with tenofovir, including frequent renal function assessments. 5. No pharmacokinetic interaction is expected; however, caution is advised as both drugs carry a risk of QT prolongation (rilpivirine at supra-therapeutic doses). 6. Co-administration may increase tenofovir alafenamide exposure. The recommended 10 mg dose with P-gp inhibitors is not feasible with Biktarvy, which contains 25 mg of tenofovir alafenamide. However, tenofovir alafenamide has a robust clinical safety profile. 7. Co-administration may increase co-medication exposure. Caution is advised due to the QT prolongation risk of both drugs. ECG monitoring is recommended. 8. Avoid co-administration of tenofovir-DF with concurrent or recent use of nephrotoxic agents. If unavoidable, closely monitor renal function. 9. Co-administration may increase co-medication exposure, but no prior dose adjustment is recommended. Caution is advised due to QT prolongation risks. ECG monitoring is recommended. 10. Co-administration may increase co-medication exposure. Caution is advised due to QT prolongation risks. ECG monitoring is recommended. Avoid co-administration for more than 14 consecutive days. 11. Co-administration may increase co-medication exposure. Use with caution and monitor with ECG. Avoid co-administration for more than 14 consecutive days. 12. Co-administration decreased co-medication exposure. Co-administration is not recommended. 13. Co-administration may increase clarithromycin exposure. Dose reduction of clarithromycin is required in patients with impaired renal function. Caution is advised due to QT prolongation risks. ECG monitoring is recommended. 14. Co-administration increased clarithromycin exposure. No adjustment is required for patients with normal renal function, but dose reductions are recommended for those with impaired renal function (reduce by 50% for CLcr 30-60 mL/min; reduce by 75% for CLcr <30 mL/min). 15. Co-administration decreased clarithromycin exposure and increased 14-OH clarithromycin exposure. The clinical significance of reduced clarithromycin is unknown. Rash occurred in 46% of uninfected individuals receiving efavirenz and clarithromycin. Consider alternatives like azithromycin. 16. Co-administration decreased clarithromycin exposure and increased 14-OH clarithromycin exposure. Nevirapine exposure was increased. Monitor for hepatic abnormalities. Due to reduced activity of the clarithromycin metabolite, overall activity may be altered. Consider alternatives like azithromycin. 17. Co-administration may increase rilpivirine exposure. Caution is advised due to QT prolongation risks (rilpivirine at supra-therapeutic doses). 18. No pharmacokinetic interaction is expected. However, caution and close monitoring are recommended due to QT prolongation risks. 19. Potential renal and hematological toxicity. Monitor renal function and hematological parameters, and consider dose reduction if required. 20. Co-administration may increase delamanid exposure. Caution is advised due to QT prolongation risks. ECG monitoring is recommended. 21. Co-administration may decrease co-medication exposure. Use with caution. 22. Potential hepatotoxicity. HLA-B5701 genotyping is recommended. 23. No pharmacokinetic interaction is expected. However, caution is advised due to QT prolongation risks. ECG monitoring is recommended. 24. Disulfiram-like reactions may occur when co-administered with metronidazole, as some ritonavir formulations (except tablets) contain alcohol. 25. No interaction is expected with lopinavir/ritonavir tablets. Co-administration is contraindicated with lopinavir/ritonavir oral solution. 26. Co-administration may decrease moxifloxacin exposure. Monitor clinical effect and increase dose if needed. Caution is advised due to QT prolongation risks. ECG monitoring is recommended. 27. Potential decreased exposure of tenofovir alafenamide. However, intracellular tenofovir diphosphate levels are likely higher than those with TDF, even without rifampicin, suggesting that TAF 25 mg QD with rifampicin, rifabutin, or rifapentine may be acceptable. 28. Co-administration increased rifabutin exposure. US HIV treatment guidelines recommend rifabutin 150 mg daily with a boosted protease inhibitor. 29. Co-administration decreased rifabutin exposure. Increase daily doses of rifabutin by 50%; consider doubling doses in regimens where rifabutin is given two or three times a week. The clinical effect of this adjustment has not been adequately evaluated. Individual tolerability and virological response should guide dose adjustments. 30. Co-administration decreased rilpivirine exposure. During co-administration with rifabutin, increase rilpivirine dose from 25 mg once daily to 50 mg once daily. After stopping rifabutin, reduce rilpivirine dose to 25 mg once daily. Maintain rilpivirine 50 mg once daily for at least two weeks after rifabutin cessation due to the persistent inducing effect. 31. Co-administration decreased zidovudine exposure. Co-administration is not recommended in the European product label for zidovudine. However, the US product label states that routine dose modification is not warranted. 32. Co-administration decreased dolutegravir concentrations. A dose adjustment to 50 mg twice daily is recommended when co-administered with rifampicin in the absence of integrase class resistance. Avoid this combination in the presence of integrase class resistance. Maintain dolutegravir 50 mg twice daily dosing for another two weeks after rifampicin cessation due to the persistent inducing effect. 33. Co-administration decreased raltegravir concentrations. The recommended dose of raltegravir when co-administered with rifampicin is 800 mg twice daily. Once-daily raltegravir is not recommended. 34. Co-administration decreased co-medication exposure. Monitor clinical effect and increase dose if needed. 35. Co-administration may decrease antiretroviral drug exposure to a moderate extent. Dose adjustment may be needed. Monitor clinical effect. Consider alternative anticonvulsants. 36. Co-administration may decrease dolutegravir exposure. The US prescribing information advises avoiding co-administration due to insufficient data for dosing recommendations. The European SPC recommends dolutegravir 50 mg twice daily but suggests alternative combinations for INSTI-resistant patients. 37. Co-administration may decrease antiretroviral drug exposure. Monitor response to antiretroviral therapy. 38. Co-administration may decrease phenobarbital and/or efavirenz exposure. Monitor therapeutic response of phenobarbital and increase dose if needed. 39. Co-administration may decrease phenytoin and antiretroviral drug exposure. Dose adjustment may be needed. Monitor clinical effect. Consider alternative anticonvulsants. 40. Co-administration may increase or decrease phenytoin and/or efavirenz concentrations. Monitor therapeutic response of phenytoin and increase dose if needed. 41. Co-administration may decrease nevirapine concentrations. Perform therapeutic drug monitoring for nevirapine if available. Consider switching to another antiretroviral agent. 42. Co-administration may increase zidovudine exposure. Routine dose modification is not warranted, but monitor closely for potential zidovudine toxicity. 43. Co-administration may increase co-medication exposure to a moderate extent. Caution is advised due to QT prolongation risks. ECG monitoring is recommended. 44. Co-administration increased metformin exposure. Assess the benefit and risk of concomitant use of bictegravir and metformin, particularly in patients with renal impairment. Monitor closely when starting co-administration in patients with moderate renal impairment due to increased lactic acidosis risk. Adjust metformin dose if required. 45. Co-administration increased metformin exposure. Adjust metformin dose when starting and stopping co-administration with dolutegravir to maintain glycemic control.
